title: Inertial Counterdiabatic Driving
authors: Julián Ferreiro-Vélez, F. A. Cárdenas-López, F. Motzoi, Xi Chen
abstract: We introduce an inertial counterdiabatic (CD) protocol that reformulates shortcut-to-adiabaticity design as a moving-frame diagonalization problem. The method employs the Magnus expansion to construct a variational propagator generated by an accessible CD ansatz. In the new rotating frame, the controls are optimized to suppress the off-diagonal Hamiltonian terms, and the CD terms are defined to counteract the corresponding inertial contribution. The propagator generated with the Magnus expansion naturally exploits additional control directions generated through its nested commutator, while the sequential design of the propagator introduces temporal nonlocality into the optimization. We benchmark the method on a two-qubit system and on the one-dimensional quantum Ising chain, where it consistently outperforms variational CD protocols based on action minimization. The largest improvements are observed near gap-closing regions, demonstrating the advantage of combining temporal and algebraic nonlocality for suppressing diabatic excitations.
summary: This paper introduces an Inertial Counterdiabatic (CD) driving protocol that improves quantum control by treating the control problem as a moving-frame diagonalization task. It uses the Magnus expansion to account for accumulated errors across time steps, surpassing standard methods. The technique is shown to be particularly effective for fast driving near quantum phase transitions in spin chain models.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of achieving high-fidelity quantum state preparation faster than the adiabatic limit using coherent control techniques.
main_result: The novel Inertial Counterdiabatic (CD) protocol consistently outperforms standard action-minimization variational CD protocols, especially near quantum gap-closing regions.
method: It reformulates the control problem as a moving-frame diagonalization problem, utilizing the Magnus expansion to construct a variational propagator that accounts for accumulated diabatic errors.
model_or_system: The method is benchmarked on a general two-qubit system and the one-dimensional quantum Ising chain, allowing for the study of controlled dynamics in interacting quantum spin systems.
key_observables: Infidelity ($1 - F(t)$), suppression of off-diagonal Hamiltonian terms, and the final ground state fidelity.
important_parameters: The optimization hyperparameters, such as the penalty coefficient ($\mu$) and the number of time discretization steps ($M$), are crucial for performance.
main_assumptions: The primary approximation involves using the Magnus expansion to approximate the time evolution operator, and the standard CD approach relies on local, instantaneous optimization.
figures_summary: Figures compare the performance of different CD schemes (Action-based vs. Inertial) and show the dependence of fidelity and control amplitude on the number of time steps ($M$) and regularization strength ($\mu$).
paper_structure: The paper introduces the general CD framework, contrasts it with standard variational methods, details the Inertial CD approach using the Magnus expansion, benchmarks it on two-qubit and Ising models, and analyzes the role of nonlocality near critical points.
why_interesting: This work provides a sophisticated, non-local theoretical tool for designing quantum control pulses, which is highly relevant for controlling complex quantum systems like superconducting qubits or trapped ions.
